Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 16:12:00 -0000
Subject: Silverpine throughput baseline & SLO targets

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the intro call today. Silverpine is sizing a dedicated inference pool for a planned public pilot in Q4. A few things we need to pin down for procurement:
- Target P95 inference latency: <= 250ms (including network)
- Typical prompt + completion length: median 120 tokens input, 300 tokens output; 95th percentile total tokens ~ 700
- Expected q1 pilot concurrency: 120 concurrent users, avg 3 requests/min per user (spikey)

Can you provide a conservative tokens-per-second estimate and an initial recommendation for GPU slab sizing (we're flexible on model family but want to keep cost predictable)?

Also looping Alex (product) and procurement for visibility.

Thanks,
Sarah Klein
Head of Product
Silverpine AI

Sarah —

Thanks, this is helpful. Quick initial read: with your median tokens ~420/request and expected concurrency pattern, the two main levers are model selection + batching strategy. A short summary of what we'll provide:
- Tokens/sec estimate: conservative steady-state ~125k t/s, peak burst up to ~450k t/s (short spikes) assuming a 7-token/ms A100-equivalent throughput for the chosen Llama2-70B-quant variant and 85% KV cache hit for repeated prefixes.
- P95 latency fit: to meet 250ms we need 1) sub-100ms scheduling overhead, 2) small micro-batches for tail requests, and 3) a burst buffer (reserved burst capacity) to absorb spikes.

I'll run a more rigorous mapping with Ben (serving) — can you confirm: expected avg tokens per request distribution (p10/p50/p90), and acceptable degraded-mode fallback (e.g., switch to 13B with slightly lower quality)? Also please confirm whether cross-region failover is required.

I'll attach a quick workbook; Ben will add GPU-slab math.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Strategic Solutions

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:18:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Silverpine throughput baseline & SLO targets

Tessa / Priyom —

I ran the numbers in the workbook. Key assumptions I used are listed inline:
- Model: Llama2-70B-quant-v2 (int8), measured baseline throughput on A100-80GB equiv: ~9.5k tokens/sec per GPU at 512 context for single-stream low-latency mode; with continuous batching (target latency cap) we can push effective aggregate tokens/sec up to ~40k per GPU while keeping P95 < 250ms for most traffic shapes.
- KV cache hit: 85% (customer indicated repeated prompts for similar templates) reduces compute ~x6 for cached steps.
- Average tokens per request: p10=80, p50=420, p90=620 (used these to derive per-request latency and tokens/sec).

Slab sizing (conservative, with 20% safety buffer):
- Steady-state requirement: 125k t/s => 125k / 40k ~= 3.1 => 4 GPUs
- Peak burst (short 1-2 minute spikes up to 450k t/s): 450k / 40k ~= 11.25 => 12 GPUs.
- Recommendation: 1 reserved slab = 8 GPUs (committed), plus ability to burst to 12 GPUs via pre-warmed on-demand nodes (ephemeral). That gives steady-state headroom and keeps committed cost reasonable.

Latency considerations:
- For low tail latency we should enforce micro-batch size <= 4 requests and enable immediate flush for single-streams; also keep sequence length padding tight.
- Quantization helps throughput but increases per-token CPU overhead slightly; cost trade-off included in workbook.

Fallback plan: automated routing to a 13B quant variant when latency constraints cannot be met — we estimate quality delta small for the pilot (customer willing to accept).

I've added a capacity diagram and CSV with measured latency profiles. See attachments.

-ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Tessa / Ben —

Thanks for the detail. A few procurement questions before we move to MPA:
1) Can you commit to P95 <= 250ms for the pilot under the committed slab (8 GPUs) or is that only with the 12 GPU burst? We need to know SLA boundaries.
2) For billing: how will burst usage be invoiced vs committed capacity?
3) Can you add an explicit safety buffer in the proposal for traffic growth (~15% month-over-month) for the first three months?

If we can see a short MPA with those guarantees and a DocuSign-ready SLA, procurement can move fast.

On the P95 question, we can accept degraded-mode fallback to the 13B model so long as the system indicates (via webhooks or headers) when fallback occurs — that visibility is important for our product team.

Thanks,
Alex Torres
Product Ops
Silverpine AI

Subject: Final: Silverpine MPA recommendation and next steps

Team / Silverpine —

Summary and ask: based on the workbook and profiles, Redwood recommends the following MPA (minimum purchase agreement) approach for the Q4 pilot:
- Committed slab: 8 GPUs (A100-equivalent) reserved for Silverpine. This covers expected steady-state with a ~20% safety margin for normal growth.
- Burst capacity: pre-warmed ephemeral pool up to 12 GPUs to absorb 1–3 minute spikes. Bursts billed at on-demand additive rate (detailed in the MPA workbook).
- SLA guarantee: P95 <= 250ms when operating on reserved slab + pre-warmed burst capacity. If pre-warmed burst is not available and we must spin to cold on-demand, P95 may exceed 250ms; that scenario will be captured as an SLA exception and subject to the agreed fallback (automatic routing to 13B quant model).
- Observability: webhook events for fallback occurrences and per-request latency headers will be included; we will add an explicit webhook for degraded-mode alerts.
- Growth buffer: 15% month-over-month allowance for the first 90 days; if exceeded, automatic notification to both parties and a light re-eval.

Next steps:
1) Ben — finalize the capacity/latency tables in the workbook and add a line-item for pre-warm costs (done).
2) Priyom — prepare MPA draft + DocuSign-ready SLA (include SLA exception language & webhook contract).
3) Sarah / Alex — confirm acceptance so procurement can sign.

I attached the SLA draft and workbook. If Silverpine agrees to the 8 GPU slab + burst to 12 model, I'll route the DocuSign to procurement today.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Strategic Solutions
Redwood Inference
